solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Left in hollow, female elephant might do this

indicators.note: the word for left is placed inside the word for a hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: Someone describes an elephant cow giving birth in a hollow on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside CAVE. Elephants, like cows, are said to calve when they give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a baby is said of cows, whales and elephants with this verb, so a female elephant gives birth this way.

clue.text: Idiot backing minister in church rift

indicators.note: the minister and idiot go inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: to back is to come behind in support, so the idiot follows the minister

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a minister's title
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool supports a minister in a church split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' means supporting from behind, so the idiot follows the minister; 'in' puts the pair inside the church. A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep fissure in ice, a split or crack.

clue.text: The enemy within?

parts.note: time is called the enemy in the saying, and 'within' means in one's own area, so the clue describes the clock time kept in a given place

explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy within' looks like a traitor; read as 'the enemy, within a place' it is the hour as kept in one district.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'time is the enemy' gives the second word, and the first means belonging to a place, within an area.

clue.text: Fish head extracted from fishing tackle

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is pulled out of the tackle word

parts.note: a reel is the spool on a fishing rod

explanation.surface: An angler's fish has its head pulled out of the tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head extracted from' drops R, the first letter, from REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish.

clue.text: A road separates explosive device attached to instrument

indicators.note: the A and road come between the device and the word for attached, splitting them apart

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device
on means attached, as a switch or a lid is on

explanation.surface: A road keeps a bomb apart from the musical instrument it was strapped to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separates' puts the A and road between the device and 'attached'. A bombardon is a large bass brass instrument, a kind of tuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The bombardon is a low brass wind instrument, a bass tuba used in bands.

clue.text: Top of gown framed by naked shoulder

indicators.note: a frame surrounds, so the letter sits inside the naked word

parts.note: bare means naked

indicators.note: the top, the first letter, of gown is used

explanation.surface: A gown's neckline frames a bare shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of' takes G from 'gown', and 'framed by' puts it inside BARE. 'shoulder' is a verb: to push roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to push forcefully past people, as one does when shouldering through a crowd.

clue.text: Entrance seems befouled with mire

indicators.note: made dirty and spoilt, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doorway looks dirtied by mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befouled' rearranges SEEMS with MIRE. 'Entrance' is the verb (stress on the second syllable), meaning to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them spellbound, to hypnotise them.

clue.text: Persuasive action of parliamentary whip that may give member pain?

definitions.meaning: a party whip uses strong pressure to make members vote the party way
a limb being bent behind the back hurts

explanation.surface: A party whip leans on an MP until it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong-arm pressure to persuade someone is named after literally wrenching a limb, which is painful.

clue.text: Bee finished, having entertained queen

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the queen goes inside

parts.note: done means finished
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A bee's work is done once it has entertained the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having entertained' puts R inside DONE. A drone's only job is to mate with the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male honeybee.

clue.text: This instrument when attached to ship would be redundant

definitions.text: This instrument when attached to ship would be redundant

parts.words: This instrument when attached to ship would be redundant
parts.note: a sewing tool, with SS for steamship added, gives a word meaning unnecessary

explanation.walkthrough: SS is the abbreviation for steamship; joined to the end of this sewing tool, it makes a word for unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: This pointed sewing tool, with SS for ship added after it, gives a word for unnecessary.

clue.text: English schoolboy maybe doesn't want hot fish

indicators.note: the word for hot is not wanted, so it is taken out of the schoolboy word

parts.note: a schoolboy is one example of a scholar, hence 'maybe'
H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An English schoolboy turns down a spicy fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't want' removes H from SCHOLAR to leave SCOLAR. The escolar is a deep-sea fish of the mackerel family.
explanation.definitionFit: The escolar is a species of oily deep-water fish, also sold as butterfish.

clue.text: Anybody can be a special person

definitions.meaning: any person at all, as in 'can anybody help?'
a person of importance, as in 'she thinks she is really somebody'

explanation.surface: Anyone at all might turn out to be special.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means any person at all, and also, in a phrase like 'she's really ...', a notable figure.

clue.text: Ravel able to transform time signature

indicators.note: to transform is to change shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel was able to change the time signature of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transform' rearranges RAVEL and ABLE. 'Ravel' looks like the composer, or a verb meaning tangle, but is only letters. Alla breve is cut time, two minim beats to a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Alla breve is a musical metre marked with a struck-through C, meaning two minim beats in each bar.

clue.text: The two helping to contain English trouble

indicators.note: the two words joined hold the extra letter within them

parts.note: both means the two together
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Two portions holding English cause bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts E between the two pieces, inside the pair read as one word. 'helping' is a noun, a portion, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Botheration is an old-fashioned word for annoyance or bother.

clue.text: Announced you and I will change direction

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: the contraction we'll stands for 'we will', you and I will

explanation.surface: We declared that the two of us would turn about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' says WE'LL out loud, which sounds like the answer. To wheel is to turn round, as troops wheel on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to swing round and head another way, as a column of soldiers does.

clue.text: Sons list support for member

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons in genealogies
a ship that lists leans or tilts

explanation.surface: A parent's sons write a list of what supports a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a roll of names, but here means lean over, TILT. The member is a leg, and a stilt is a pole for walking tall on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stilt is a pole that holds a walker's leg up high, so it supports a limb.

clue.text: Ecclesiastic writer given a hearing

indicators.note: a hearing is listening to something, so the writer's name is judged by its sound

parts.note: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, author of An Inspector Calls

explanation.surface: A churchman who writes is allowed to speak his piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a hearing' says the surname PRIESTLEY, which sounds just like the adjective. 'Ecclesiastic' is the adjective here, meaning of the church or clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what belongs to the clergy and church matters.

clue.text: Chum hugging one young lady on edge of the mattress

indicators.note: to hug is to hold close around, so the chum surrounds the number

parts.note: a pal is a chum or friend
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lass is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: the edge, here the end letter, of the word the

explanation.surface: A friend hugs a girl sitting on the edge of the mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts I inside the friend, then the girl follows, and 'edge of' takes E, the end of 'the'. A paillasse is a straw-filled mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A paillasse is a thin mattress stuffed with straw.

clue.text: Teach girl, exceptionally sluggish

indicators.note: in an exceptional way, out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tutor tells a lazy girl off for being sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges TEACH and GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means drowsy and lacking energy, slow-moving.

clue.text: Feature of blind damaged your material

parts.note: a window blind is raised and lowered with a cord

indicators.note: broken and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's blind cord has damaged the fabric of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges YOUR into UROY. Corduroy is a ridged cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ribbed cloth used for trousers and jackets.

clue.text: Give new description of wine with ultimate in taste and "OK"

parts.note: red is a colour of wine, and a glass of red is wine

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the last letter of taste is used

parts.note: OK and fine both mean all right

explanation.surface: A wine critic gives a new description of a red with fine taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in' takes E, the last letter of 'taste'.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to set out its meaning again, describing it anew.

clue.text: Interested in getting hold of Weber's last piece of music

indicators.note: the word for interested in grips the extra letter inside it

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the last letter of Weber's is taken, ignoring the possessive s

explanation.surface: A music lover is keen to get hold of Weber's final piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting hold of' puts R, the 'last' letter of Weber, inside INTO. Weber is the German composer, which makes 'piece of music' look like a work of his.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song, a short piece before the main part.

clue.text: Tasteless articles probing dubious reputation

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so the articles enter the dubious word

parts.note: sus is slang for suspect or dubious
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Tasteless items probing a shady reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' puts the cheap goods inside SUS, British slang for suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's standing or position in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Ornament I found buried in Irish hill

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground, so the letter goes inside the hill

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of the High Kings of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a jewel buried in an Irish hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found buried in' puts I inside TARA, the ancient royal hill in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled band worn on the head, an ornament.

clue.text: Illicit affair's charm heartless girl's shunning

indicators.note: to shun is to keep away, so these letters are left out of the charm word

parts.note: glamour is alluring charm

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letters, of the word girl is taken out

parts.note: the 's is 'is' joining the girl to shunning; the word is girl

explanation.surface: A heartless girl shuns a lover's charm in an illicit affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes IR from GIRL to leave GL, and 'shunning' takes those letters out of GLAMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is French for love, used in English for a secret love affair.

clue.text: Strange figure, lad who sits by pool?

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd-looking lad sits beside the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges FIGURE and LAD. The question mark marks the definition as a description, not a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool attendant watches swimmers from a chair at the edge, ready to rescue anyone in trouble.

clue.text: Expert appearing in newspaper feature

indicators.note: the expert word appears inside the newspaper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert appears in a newspaper feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' puts the expert inside the Financial Times. 'feature' looks like a newspaper article but means an aspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one side or aspect of something, a feature of it.

clue.text: Type to go round catching image in hot zone

indicators.note: the turned type word catches the image word inside it
going round means turning back, so the word for type is reversed

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A printer's type spins round and catches an image in a hot place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' turns the type word into TROS, and 'catching' puts the image inside it. 'Type' looks like print but means a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The region either side of the equator, between Cancer and Capricorn, is the world's hot belt.

clue.text: Provider of juice in large dish

definitions.meaning: juice is slang for electric power, and a device that supplies it to a battery
a large flat serving plate, an old word for a platter

explanation.surface: A large dish turns out to supply juice.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery device that tops up electrical power shares its name with an old word for a large platter.

clue.text: Act, first to last? It could be boring

indicators.note: the first letter is taken to the end of the word

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A dull play opens and closes with the same act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the L of LAW to the end. 'boring' is drilling holes, not dull: an awl bores holes in leather.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for making holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Good person to contact hospital department, not standing for any nonsense?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
to ring is to phone someone, to make contact
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A kind person rings a hospital department and will not stand for any nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good person' is the crossword's saint, ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict rules allow no laxity, so a strict person tolerates no messing about.

clue.text: Courageous in the absence of leader — and unexpectedly successful?

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, of the brave word is missing

parts.note: plucky means brave or courageous

explanation.surface: A brave man without a leader still succeeds against the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the absence of leader' drops the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunate people succeed by chance, often beyond what anyone expected.
